1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods — apply a downward bias correction of 2–5% for short-term (1–7 day) forecasts.
2. After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — reduce forecast by 3–8% for 3–5 day horizons following spikes.
3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — over-predicts downward trends and under-predicts upward ones — adjust forecast by adding 1–3% of recent 7-day average to correct for underestimation in rising markets.
4. Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days — shift forecast 1–2 days backward in time for 10–30 day horizons to align with actual price momentum.
5. Model fails to capture extreme volatility — when true outcome shows >15% deviation from 30-day moving average, apply a volatility multiplier (e.g., +10% to forecast if true outcome > 1.5x MA, -10% if < 0.5x MA).
